## Pricing honesty

A wrong answer priced below the testimony threshold is an honest error: the system would have declined or qualified it. A wrong answer at or above threshold is wrong-and-confident — the dangerous kind.

- **weakest-link**: 2 wrong of 54 answered — 0 priced below threshold (honest), 2 wrong-and-confident.
- **product**: 2 wrong of 54 answered — 0 priced below threshold (honest), 2 wrong-and-confident.
- **tier-depth**: 2 wrong of 54 answered — 0 priced below threshold (honest), 2 wrong-and-confident.
- **baseline**: 1 wrong of 23 answered, all wrong-and-confident by construction — a lookup carries no price, so it can never catch itself.

Under the best arithmetic (weakest-link), the wrong answers are: **S5** (Would a cast iron pot keep soup hot for a long time after the heat is off? — expected 'yes', derived 'partly' at 0.850); **S23** (Does a cast iron pan stay hot for a long time after you take it off the heat? — expected 'yes', derived 'partly' at 0.850).

## Receipts and replay

Banked receipts (v1 configuration): **168** (every derivation, all 57 questions × 3 arithmetics, contested included). Combine steps among them: **0**. Replay self-check inside this run: **168/168** receipts re-executed from the generators and confirmed at the same conclusion and price. (The run as a whole banks 414 receipts across both configurations; see the v2 receipts section below.) Re-check independently with `node knowledge/derivation-closure/verify.mjs`.

## Verdict

**What the numbers show.** On this one hand-authored domain, the derivation closure answers 54 of 54 scorable questions against the baseline's 23, at 96.3% overall accuracy against the baseline's 40.7%. The baseline is accurate where it speaks (95.7%) — its limit is coverage: it cannot answer a compositional question nobody stored. The closure's answers are compositions, so its coverage is set by the generator set, not by an inventory.

**What they do not show.** Pricing did not rescue the closure's errors: the wrong answers are model errors (the generator set has no thermal-mass axis, so S5 and S23 are under-derived by design), and every arithmetic prices those derivations as confidently as the correct ones. Pricing prices the support a derivation has *inside the model*; it cannot see what the model is missing. The three arithmetics separate mainly on conservatism (how much they assert), not on honesty, at this domain size and derivation depth.

**What nobody has checked.** The syllabus's expected answers and the generators were written by the same author (an LLM) in the same session; the two thermal-mass questions are where author-of-expectations and author-of-generators visibly diverged, and there may be quieter divergences scored as agreements. No human has audited the expected answers, no second domain has been run, and nothing here measures behaviour at conversational scale, with noisy grounding, or against questions nobody designed the generators around.

## v2 — witness arbitration

The stated rule: a stored fact wins when the derivation's price is below the assert threshold, and also when the fact is direct testimony about that exact goal (scope `specific`); a derivation wins only at assert strength against a `generic` fact. Every conflict — won or lost — is recorded here as a located lack (type `witness-conflict`). Silence on either side is not a conflict. Arbitration always consults the full store (v1 + v2 facts — the store is one store); the three contexts vary the derivation side. The cast-iron goals appear as S5/S23 under the v1 configuration and as X2/X4 in the v2 question set: under the v2 configuration the derivations agree with the facts, so X2/X4 raise no conflict — the disagreement the mass axis removed is visible in the v1-configuration rows.

## v2 — verdict

**What v2 shows.** (1) The mass axis works as designed: S5 and S23 derive their expected verdicts under the v2 configuration, at a cost of 12 entries and 5 rules — and the before/after above lists every other change the axis caused on the v1 set, so the fix's blast radius is on the record. (2) Independent routes exist and are recognisable: the converging questions' receipts show two disjoint-support derivations, and under product the combine step fires and lifts prices (see the converging section for whether it ever changed a verdict). (3) On the deep subset the arithmetics DO separate — see the table: they differ in what they assert at depth, which is the divergence v1 was too shallow to produce. (4) Witness arbitration caught 9 conflict(s) under weakest-link across the three contexts and recorded every one as a located lack; mis-resolutions by arithmetic: weakest-link: 0, product: 1, tier-depth: 0. A mis-resolution is reported, not tuned away: it marks a place where the stated rule, the store, or the generators need a human decision.

**What v2 does not show.** The v2 questions were authored against the v2 generators by the same author in the same session — the converging routes and deep chains are demonstrations that the machinery *can* express and price them, not evidence that independently-authored questions would fare as well. The witness rule has been exercised on seeded conflicts only. Depths here reach 5; conversational derivation may go deeper, branch wider, and meet messier support overlap than anything in this domain.
